content.text: Fipsen is a unique northern German trick-taking game, traditionally played in the coastal regions between Hamburg and Bremen. It belongs to the 'One vs. All' family of games, similar to Nap or Skat. Fipsen is distinguished by its highly specialized 25-card deckâ€”where the 7 of Diamonds (the 'Rute') is the only card of its suit allowedâ€”and its aggressive doubling mechanics. The game is a test of risk management, where players bid on the number of tricks they can win using a limited hand of just five cards.

Fipsen originated in the 19th century as a favorite game among farmers and sailors in Northern Germany. While its popularity has waned since the midnd20th century, it remains a cultural centerpiece in the town of Prisdorf, where Fipsen tournaments are held alongside Skat events.
4 players (standard). Each player plays for themselves, but three act as a temporary team against the highest bidder.
25 cards. Start with a 32ndcard Skat deck and remove all Diamonds except the Seven of Diamonds.

Each player receives 5 cards (traditionally 3 then 2). Two cards are dealt face-down to the center (the Skat). Three cards are left over and set aside.
